A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same functional-attribution method for mechanistic anomaly detection. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports original vision and language-model detection experiments, toy-model validation, sensitivity analyses, and trusted-set contamination tests.

after.justification: V2 retains those original empirical results and adds adversarial-example detection results for four attacks in Appendix E.4.

M1.justification: The SGLD sampling procedure, prediction-based observables, coupling measures, aggregation strategies, and offline UMAP K-NN detector remain unchanged. The added deployment suggestions do not establish a revision to the implemented method.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates targeted PGD examples within a backdoored CIFAR-10 model's multi-pathology experiment. V2 additionally evaluates PGD, FGSM, AutoAttack, and Square examples on a clean CIFAR-10 model, extending attack-scenario coverage while retaining the existing datasets and tasks.

E2.justification: The BackdoorBench, language-model, and OpenOOD comparator sets are unchanged. New Table 8 contains only the proposed detector's results across attack scenarios; it introduces no competing detection methods.

E3.justification: New Appendix E.4 introduces evaluation on a clean ResNet-18/CIFAR-10 model using offline UMAP K-NN and the backdoor experiments' hyperparameters. Existing protocols remain unchanged, including the backdoored-model PGD experiment. Section 6's deployment threshold suggestions are not reported as implemented evaluation changes.

E4.justification: The toy-model validation, hyperparameter and sample-size sweeps, trusted-set contamination tests, and mechanism case studies are unchanged. New Appendix E.4 adds attack-detection benchmark scores, without a separate ablation, detector-evasion test, or error analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same five-seed toy-model reporting, five-subsample trusted-set analysis, and Wilcoxon tests. The new adversarial table supplies point estimates without adding run counts, uncertainty estimates, or statistical tests.

E6.justification: V2 Table 8 adds detection AUROCs of 0.982 for PGD, 0.880 for FGSM, 0.972 for AutoAttack, and 0.888 for Square. These are additional clean-model results, not same-setting improvements over V1's backdoored-model experiment. Previously reported numerical and graphical results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 4.2 and Appendix A retain the same Laplace approximation, cross-subspace orthogonality proposition, energy-distribution definitions, assumptions, and detection-condition derivation. Updating the Kreer citation does not change the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract now describes evidence beyond backdoors as preliminary. The corresponding introduction contribution likewise becomes tentative and drops its broad near-perfect-accuracy assertion. The central functional-attribution contribution and backdoor-performance claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 6 adds concrete deployment considerations: screening with a cheaper latent-space detector before functional confirmation, false-positive versus false-negative tradeoffs, and choosing thresholds using trusted-data false-positive rates or running test-score statistics. General complementarity and computational-cost limitations were already discussed in V1.

D1.justification: Section 5 adds an explicit project-code repository link, absent from V1. New Appendix E.4 specifies reuse of backdoor-experiment hyperparameters. Existing implementation details, training settings, hardware information, and timing tables are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for FGSM, AutoAttack, and Square: Goodfellow et al. (2015), Croce and Hein (2020), and Andriushchenko et al. (2020). Research positioning remains largely unchanged; the Kreer and Mallen bibliographic revisions update already-cited works.

P1.justification: Changes are localized to abstract and contribution wording, expanded deployment discussion, publication and bibliographic metadata, and the inserted Appendix E.4 subsection. Quirky Models and Detailed BackdoorBench Results become E.5 and E.6; the overall narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds the four-row adversarial-results Table 8. The previous detailed BackdoorBench Table 8 becomes Table 9 and moves to the top of the final page alongside continuing prose. Existing figures are unchanged, with otherwise limited layout reflow.

improvement.justification: V2 better qualifies its broader generalization claims, adds supporting adversarial-detection evidence, and improves practical guidance and code-access information. The gains are limited: the new experiment omits attack budgets, sample counts, and uncertainty reporting, while the principal methods, theory, and existing results remain unchanged.
